title: Internal docs: automated regional failover behavior, runbook links, and controlled-test customer symptoms
author: Tomáš Novák
body:
Summary
This PR updates internal-facing documentation to reflect the new regional failover automation behavior (trigger engine + orchestrator state machine), where to look during incidents/tests (dashboards + audit trail), and what customers may see during controlled failover tests. It also standardizes language for Support/CS escalations to avoid over-promising while giving concrete troubleshooting guidance.

Context
Recent incident threads and SUP tickets highlighted gaps in how we explain (a) monitor-only vs active automation, (b) progressive failover behavior by tier/route/model, and (c) customer-visible symptoms during controlled tests (e.g., brief connection resets, elevated tail latency, occasional 429/load-shed depending on tier). This is paired with the rollout plan that gates production enablement behind feature flags and on-call approvals.

What changed
- Added a new internal doc page: “Automated regional failover: expected behavior and operator workflow”
  - Defines terms: degraded vs failed, monitor-only vs active, progressive failover stages (canary %, tier/route scope)
  - Links to the runbook and dashboards
  - Explicitly documents manual override policy and RBAC expectations (who can flip modes / emergency disable)
- Updated the on-call handbook section: “During regional impairment”
  - Step-by-step: verify signals → check orchestrator state → confirm safe-to-failover gates → comms → rollback conditions
  - Adds a “don’t do this” list (avoid flappy toggles; don’t fail over without capacity checks)
- Added “Controlled failover tests: what customers may see” (internal + Support macro copy)
  - Expected symptoms (by request type): chat streaming vs non-streaming, embeddings vs generation
  - Differentiates Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (where supported)
  - Includes guidance on logs to request, and when to escalate to SRE vs Platform
- Added a short “FAQ for enterprise escalations” section
  - Clarifies we do not guarantee zero impact during controlled tests; we limit blast radius, use canaries, and have abort criteria
  - Explains audit trail availability and what we can share externally

Customer-visible symptoms (controlled test window)
- Possible: brief spike in p95/p99 latency (seconds), intermittent stream reconnects, occasional 5xx bursts during the routing transition window, and/or temporary 429 if load shedding engages.
- Not expected: sustained elevated error rate after stabilization window; cross-region data leakage; changes to auth behavior.
- Notes:
  - Streaming: customer may observe partial chunks followed by disconnect; client should retry with idempotency key where supported.
  - Function/tool calls: may see increased timeouts if a request spans a routing transition; recommend higher client-side total timeout during test window if customer opts-in.

Operational notes
- These docs assume the orchestrator is either in monitor-only or active mode; enabling active mode in prod still requires release gating + on-call approval.
- Runbook section links point to: Automated Region Failover Runbook (internal) and Failover Dashboards/Alerts (internal). Please keep links internal-only.

Rollout
- Intended to land before the next production controlled failover (low-risk slice). Support macros included but not yet published to the external help center.

Screenshots
- Included updated dashboard screenshot placeholders (internal-only) and an example audit trail snippet.

Testing
- Link-checker run for internal docs; docs build + spellcheck.

Related
- Linear: ENG-2851 (prod controlled failover), ENG-2847 (dashboards), PM-612 (customer narrative)
- Jira: SUP-19288/SUP-19312 (customer questions + streaming disconnect symptoms)

Notes for reviewers
- Please focus on accuracy of symptom descriptions and ensuring language is consistent with our change management policy (manual override + hold-down timers; not promising instant failover).
commits: docs: add internal page for automated regional failover behavior + operator workflow
docs: add controlled failover test symptoms + support macro copy
docs: update on-call handbook regional impairment section with state machine checks
docs: link dashboards/runbook and add audit trail references
chore: fix linkcheck failures + glossary updates
review_conversation: Aisha Bello: The symptom list is good, but can we explicitly tie load shedding (429) to the ‘degraded but available’ mode and mention it’s tier-aware? Also please avoid implying burn-rate alerts page on its own will trigger failover.

Tomáš Novák (author): Updated: 429/load shed is now explicitly described as a graceful degradation control and noted as tier-aware. Also clarified alerts are signals only; orchestrator decisions are based on the trigger engine + safety checks (capacity/dependency) and on-call mode.

Mina Haddad: Please add a sentence that progressive failover can be scoped by route/model and that we may keep a subset pinned to the original region for validation during game day. Also remove the word ‘instant’ anywhere near DNS/edge changes.

Tomáš Novák (author): Done. Added route/model scoping note in ‘progressive failover stages’ and removed ‘instant’ wording; replaced with ‘within propagation window; verify via dashboard + sample requests’.

Dev Patel: Support macro copy: can we add a short checklist of what to ask for (request IDs, timestamps, region header if present, whether streaming) and a clear escalation path? Also the enterprise FAQ should say we can provide a post-test readout upon request (internal approval).

Tomáš Novák (author): Added Support checklist + escalation guidance (Support → SRE on-call for impact confirmation; Platform Routing for policy questions). Updated enterprise FAQ: ‘post-test summary available upon request with account team + SRE approval’.

Connor O'Brien: Please align with release gating language: active mode enabling requires release eng sign-off and on-call approval. Also add the rollback expectation: we must be able to revert at any stage of progressive failover.
Tomáš Novák (author): Updated ‘Operational notes’ and ‘Rollout’ sections to match release gating. Added explicit rollback-at-any-stage statement and pointed to runbook rollback section.
Felix Schneider: The audit trail snippet is useful; can you add where to find it in the console and note retention limitations? (Internal-only note).
Tomáš Novák (author): Added: console path and current retention window note (subject to change; internal).
Connor O'Brien: Approved with nit addressed.
release_notes: Internal documentation only: adds operator workflow + support macro guidance for automated regional failover and controlled failover tests; no customer-facing docs shipped.
